diagnoses.summary: PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with significant temperature rise and pressure deviation in the CSTR. The strongest rule-based hints point to an exothermic upset likely caused by the CSTR heater behaving abnormally or a loss of catalyst activity, with secondary possibilities involving H2 PCV issues.
PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with strong evidence of a sensor fault driving SPE; secondary candidates include H2 PCV issues and reactor temperature/pressure anomalies.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong high-temperature signals and a saturated temperature control loop, plus a dominant SPE contribution from the TIC measurement. This points to a reactor temperature upset driven by an actuator fault (heater) or a TIC sensor fault, with possible concurrent process effects.

PCA flag indicates a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. The strongest evidence points to an up-stream actuator driving an excessive reactor temperature, with possible catalyst-related effects contributing to the observed acetone/temperature signals.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong temperature rise in the CSTR and high temperature alarms (R_T_H, R_T_HH) along with a saturated R_TIC loop. The most consistent fault is an actuator fault at the CSTR heater causing excessive heating and triggering the high-temp alarms, with secondary contributions from catalyst activity loss and a saturated control loop.
High-energy, coherent upset with reactor temperature rising and loop R_TIC saturated; strongest indication of an actuator fault affecting the CSTR heater.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset dominated by the CSTR temperature rise with strong high-temperature alarms and a saturated temperature control loop; two plausible fixed faults point to the CSTR heater forcing the temperature up or a loss of catalyst activity increasing the intrinsic reaction heat.

PCA detects a large, coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violated, with reactor pressure-related signals dominating. The most consistent explanation is H2 PCV (vent) impairment causing pressure rise and compensatory control activity upstream/downstream. Several PCV-related faults are plausible (capacity degradation or stuck valve), supported by the dominant cstr_pressure_bar contribution and saturated safety/PI loops.

PCA shows large coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violations; strongest evidence points to a H2 PCV (vent) related fault causing reactor pressure abnormality and control loop saturation at RB_LIC. Among catalogue faults, the H2 PCV issues best explain the dominant cstr_pressure_bar contribution and the saturated RB_LIC loop behavior.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T2 and SPE violations and a saturated RB_LIC loop. The most consistent fault is an actuator limitation at the CSTR outlet/column feed path causing flow restriction, with other faults less likely but plausible given the disturbances observed.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous SPE violations. Top contributors point to reactor temperature/heater dynamics and associated control actions, with the strongest rule-based indication being a heater issue on the CSTR. The most plausible single fault is a heater-related failure causing abnormal reactor temperature behavior, consistent with high T² and SPE together with the rule-based hypothesis of reactor heater stuck high.
The PCA indicates a large coherent upset with strong T2 and SPE; most evidence points to an actuator fault in the CSTR heater causing the reactor temperature to rise despite control action.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with simultaneous high T² and high SPE, with an alarm on DIST_X_L and a saturated RB_LIC loop. Among catalogue faults, the most plausible single cause is condenser cooling loss driving the distillation column behavior abnormality.

PCA abnormal with high T² and high SPE indicating a coherent plant upset with some sensor correlations broken. Rule-based hints point to a heater fault driving a high reactor temperature, with possible secondary effects on catalyst activity and condenser cooling.

PCA flags a large, coherent plant upset with strong contribution from reactor temperature and related variables, with notable SPE indicating new correlation patterns. Rule-based hints also point toward catalyst/heat-up related faults and condenser tradeoffs. Most likely multiple interacting faults; primary suspicion is catalyst- or heater-related process upset propagating through the CSTR.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by higher reactor temperature and CSTR pressure dynamics, with heater-related faulty command feedback highly plausible. Likely a control/actuator fault at the CSTR heater, with secondary process-related faults contributing.

High coherence upset with large temperature driver and elevated reboiler holdup suggests a heater actuator fault causing reactor temperature rise; other plausible contributing faults exist but reactor heater issue is most likely.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by a surge in CSTR temperature and related process variables. The strongest rule-based signals point to a heater issue causing an elevated reactor temperature, with additional hints of catalyst/reaction-rate effects and H2 PCV-related issues as secondary possibilities.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violated. Top contributors point to CSTR temperature signal and reboiler holdup, with secondary hints from CSTR pressure and upstream controller actions.-Based on fixed-rule tendencies, the most likely immediate faults are actuator issues in the CSTR heater or related process upsets, followed by catalyst/activity and reboiler leaks.

A large, coherent plant upset with significant T² and SPE violations. The strongest indicators point to a reactor-side disturbance (high reactor temperature) with a contributing issue on the reboiler side. Faults in the catalyst/condensation area are less supported by the primary contributors.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by CSTR temperature rise and pressure signals. Rule-based hints point to an actuator-related root at the CSTR heater, with secondary possibilities including catalyst/activity issues and reboiler/leak/gas handling anomalies. Most likely: reactor_heater_stuck_high.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with significant temperature rise in the CSTR and related upstream/downstream adjustments; multiple fault hypotheses point to reactor heat input/chemistry issues and a downstream cooling/condensation interaction.
PCA signals a large, coherent process upset with strong contribution from reboiler variables; most likely a reboiler liquid leak causing rising reboiler holdup and associated control action.
